handled_verified._description: DERIVED BY SOURCE REFERENCE, NOT YET BY PROBE — read this before quoting the list. A type is in this bucket when src/ast/real-vb-analyzer.ts NAMES it as a quoted literal in code position (comments and template literals stripped; .tmp-f48/cov/node-refs.mts). That is a NECESSARY condition for the node being handled and NOT a sufficient one: a name appearing in an evidence-classification helper or a read-side filter is not an emission. The stronger instrument — script/m14/completeness-inventory.ts section A with a `--verify-silence` pass that re-parses live code — has NOT been run for vb, and the only committed proof of emission for this lane is the five fixtures under validation/m14/fixtures/vb/ plus the whole-population run in `coverage` below. Treat this bucket as a worklist with its method declared, not a verdict.

internal_silent._description: The complement of handled_verified: 21 of the 166 distinct named node types are NEVER NAMED by src/ast/real-vb-analyzer.ts. NOT VERIFIED SILENT — several (aggregate_clause/group_by_clause/join_clause/let_clause are LINQ query syntax; date_literal; tuple_expression) look like real content rather than literals or wrappers, which is exactly the class a completeness audit exists to catch. They are listed here so that every named type is in exactly one bucket and none is silently absent; the silence itself is OWED, not measured.

THE SURFACE IS ABSENT ON ALL THREE AXES AND EACH WAS MEASURED SEPARATELY rather than inferred from one: the GRAMMAR has no such production; the ROUTER routes no markup file to this lane; and the CORPUS holds none — 0 tracked `.aspx`, 0 `.ascx`, 0 `.vbhtml`, 0 `.master` over every repository in the corpus root (measured 2026-10-28 by `git ls-files` per repository). The 58 admitted `.vb` files are code-behind and library sources, and a rendered component is a MARKUP construct that VB.NET's grammar does not express. THE NEAREST CODE CONSTRUCT IS CONSTRUCTION AND IS ALREADY PUBLISHED: `new_expression` / object creation is `instantiates` (459 edges), which is instantiation, not rendering. R2 (a grammar patch) is unavailable IN PRINCIPLE here: a patched node would fire on 0 sites, because no source in the admitted population writes a markup tag. excluded.label: mixes_in
excluded.from: VB-D2 (2026-10-28) — GRAMMAR-ABSENCE, 0 of the 168 named node types match the mixin/composition stem scan (mixin|trait|with_clause|embed). THE NEAR MISSES ARE MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED: VB's two composition surfaces are `Inherits` and `Implements`, and BOTH ARE ALREADY PUBLISHED as the supertype/conformance relations they are — extends 32 edges, implements 82 edges over the 58-file population (`script/m14/residual-gate.ts --lane vb`, 2026-10-28). The third candidate is `Partial`, measured 2 occurrences over the same 58 files: a partial declaration SPLITS one unit across files, so its row would be X→X, and the fleet's own precedent refuses that (csharp's `partial`; scala's self-type information test). VB has NO mixin: a `Module`'s members are brought into scope by `Imports`, which is a NAME-RESOLUTION directive and adds no member to any type, and no VB construct composes another type's members without inheritance or implementation. FALSIFIER: an admitted site where a VB declaration acquires another type's MEMBERS without `Inherits`/`Implements` — 0 measured.

excluded.label: part_of
excluded.from: VB-D3 (2026-10-28) — GRAMMAR-ABSENCE, 0 of the 168 named node types is a part-inclusion production (stem scan part|include|fragment|split). `#Include` DOES NOT EXIST IN VB.NET — measured 0 occurrences of `#Include` or `Include(` over the 58-file population — and `Partial` (2) is the X→X split already rejected in VB-D2. `#Region` is a folding directive that names no unit at all. The fleet's `part_of` names ANOTHER UNIT AS A PART, sharing one scope and importing nothing (the rust `mod`-vs-`include` ruling, L-2026-10-21-06); VB has no textual inclusion of any kind, which is also why `#Include` absence is a language fact rather than a corpus fact. FALSIFIER: any admitted `.vb` site carrying an inclusion directive the wired grammar parses into a node — 0 measured.

_extended_types_2026_10_28._question: the four extended relationship values are the whole of this lane's gap; one is now IMPLEMENTED and three are RULED with a class, a count and a falsifier
_extended_types_2026_10_28.decorates: IMPLEMENTED (VB-D0). 209 edges over the 58-file admitted population through the production path (`parseFile`, direct walk — the residual arm prints only the ten types the spec listed before this change, so its closure could not show the eleventh; this count is the direct measurement). Source = the DECORATED DECLARATION, target = the attribute's LEAF (`System.Serializable` -> `Serializable`) because the arbiter binds by name against the project, and the written spelling rides in `metadata.attributeName`. Metadata per row: attributeName, attributeLeaf, attributeForm, argumentCount, decoratedKind, resolved. THE HOLDER IS RESOLVED BY A BOUNDED CLIMB (field_declaration / declaration_statement only): a field's symbol is published from its DECLARATOR while the grammar puts `repeat(field("attributes", $.attribute_list))` on the DECLARATION, so a declarator-only read loses every field attribute (measured shape: `<_a, _b_>` is one declaration, two declarators, two rows). Fixture: validation/m14/fixtures/vb/attributes-as-decorations.vb (+ expectation), whose forbid rows pin the three defects a naive emission produces: the attribute's ARGUMENT read as a second attribute, attributes leaking from an enclosing type onto a member, and the attribute name returning to `references` (which `inAttributePosition` suppresses by an earlier differential finding). All 209 rows carry `resolved: false` because the framework attribute types are not declared in these projects — a measured wall, ruled in the incoming declaration, NOT laundered as external.
